summary: Fleet R0 reclaim authority + R1 effect-fence binding, one branch. R0: rolling-TTL renew (renew = now + extend, non-cumulative), expiry becomes the single fence authority, begin_run fails closed on an expired lease, expired/force reclaim goes through CAS with recorded justification. R1: the effect execution path (subagent runner, tool execution journal, five builtin effect tools) is bound to the lease fence so expiry actually stops effects. Also adopts the R0 spec test file that had lived untracked in the main tree and survived the 14:26 reset only because untracked.

No second store, no heartbeat or liveness controller, no new takeover policy owner.

g1.necessity: Before R0, renew accumulated TTL instead of recomputing now + extend, so a once-renewed lease could outlive any liveness bound; expiry was not the single fence authority; begin_run did not fail closed on an expired lease; and expired/force reclaim lacked the CAS-with-justification path, leaving reclaim authority ambiguous under races. Without these, R1 fences have no authoritative expiry to enforce.

g2.non_duplication: No second store, no second coordination authority, no heartbeat or liveness controller. The same FleetStore CAS remains the single mutation authority; this tranche changes the renew/expiry/reclaim semantics inside it.
